title: Reduce OPD waiting time at district hospitals
notice: Simulated demonstration data — not an official government record.

challenge.outcome_statement: Cut median wait from registration to first clinician contact, with no extra sanctioned staff and no change to the existing HMIS.
challenge.kpi_definition: Median of (first clinician contact − registration) over all OPD visits in the window, from existing registration and consultation timestamps.
challenge.baseline_source: District hospital OPD registration and consultation timestamps (HMIS export)
challenge.baseline_method: All 61,480 OPD visits Oct–Dec 2025; visits missing either timestamp (3.1%) excluded and reported.
challenge.comparison_unit: Second district hospital OPD with no deployment

criteria.kpi: Writes to the HMIS of record

milestones.title: Sandbox provisioned, baseline re-measured
milestones.evidence_expected: Independent baseline study, signed by the Civil Surgeon

milestones.title: Instrumentation live, read-only confirmed
milestones.evidence_expected: Access log extract showing zero writes to the HMIS

milestones.title: 90-day operating window complete
milestones.evidence_expected: Raw timestamp dataset, analysis notebook, deviation log

milestones.title: Exit, data deletion certified
milestones.evidence_expected: Deletion certificate under the exit annexure

steps.note: The programme desk re-derives 94 minutes from the raw HMIS export before anything is published. No baseline, no challenge.

baseline.result: 94 min reproduced from the raw export; 3.1% of visits excluded for missing timestamps, as stated.

steps.action: Sealed and published the success criteria
steps.note: The baseline and four KPI targets are hashed with SHA-256 and published. Changing any of them later breaks the seal.

steps.action: Set the risk envelope and screened applicants
steps.note: Five startups applied. Two fail hard filters, one is eligible only under standard conditions. Every result carries its reason.

risk.users: One OPD, staff only; no patient-facing change
risk.systems: Read-only access to registration and consultation timestamps
risk.data: Pseudonymised timestamps; no names, no clinical data
risk.reversibility: Beacons removed in a day; HMIS untouched
risk.exit_cost: Nil beyond the M4 deletion certificate
risk.relaxation: GFR 173(i) prior-turnover and experience waivers apply within this cap

screening.name: QueueSense Systems
screening.why: DPIIT-recognised; read-only design sits inside the risk cap; 173(i) relaxation applies.

screening.name: Setu Health Queue
screening.why: DPIIT-recognised; SMS nudges inside the cap. No live deployment yet — evidence is a replay only.

screening.name: CareBridge Enterprise
screening.why: Not DPIIT-recognised, so 173(i) does not reach it; eligible only on standard turnover conditions.

screening.name: MedFlow Analytics
screening.why: Hard filter: needs write access to the HMIS, which the risk envelope forbids.

screening.name: ShikshaTrack Labs
screening.why: Hard filter: requires live personal data across districts; outside the data class.

steps.note: Three evaluators score against published weights. The ranking explains itself; the panel, not a model, decides.

evaluation.weights: Outcome fit 40 · Evidence quality 25 · Data risk 20 · Delivery capacity 15

scores.name: QueueSense Systems
scores.why: Two trust hospitals, median wait down 41% over 90 days; read-only.

scores.name: Setu Health Queue
scores.why: Strong Marathi-first design; evidence is a historical replay, not a deployment.

scores.name: CareBridge Enterprise
scores.why: Proven hardware; weaker outcome evidence; standard terms only.

evaluation.dissent: One evaluator asked that M2 prove zero HMIS writes from logs, not a declaration. Adopted.

steps.action: Awarded the pilot and signed the pilot design
steps.note: The panel's choice is recorded with the design it was awarded on: sandbox, data and IP terms, and four paid milestones.

startup.name: QueueSense Systems
startup.capability: Token-free OPD flow from anonymous BLE beacons and existing registration timestamps. Read-only.
startup.prior_evidence: 2 trust hospitals; median wait down 41% over 90 days.

design.scope: One district hospital OPD, 90 days, staff-facing only
design.sandbox: Isolated read replica of registration and consultation timestamps
design.data_access: Pseudonymised timestamps only; no patient identifiers leave the hospital network
design.ip: Startup keeps product IP; the department keeps the data and a perpetual licence to the pilot reports
design.cybersecurity: Read-only DB role; access logged; CERT-In incident reporting within 6 hours

steps.note: Each artefact is hashed when it is submitted. The hash, not a covering letter, is what reviewers check later.

evidence.title: Independent baseline re-measurement
evidence.content: Baseline study, Oct–Dec 2025: median 94 min, p95 212 min, n = 59,574 visits with both timestamps. Signed: Civil Surgeon (simulated).

evidence.title: HMIS access-log extract, days 1–20
evidence.content: Role qs_readonly: 41,906 SELECT, 0 INSERT, 0 UPDATE, 0 DELETE between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-03 (simulated extract).

steps.note: Acceptance completes the payment packet. From here the payment clock is visible to everyone.

steps.action: Paid milestone 1; recorded milestone 2 as delayed
steps.note: One payment on time, one late — and the late one carries its reason and an open grievance clock instead of disappearing.

milestones.1.payment.delay_reason: Budget head re-appropriation pending with the treasury

steps.note: The 90-day dataset goes to the validator untouched. The exit certificate proves the startup's copy of the data is gone.

evidence.title: Analysis notebook and deviation log
evidence.content: analysis.ipynb; deviations: beacon outage 2026-02-18 (6 h), excluded and disclosed (simulated).

evidence.title: Data deletion certificate
evidence.source: QueueSense Systems, countersigned by hospital IT
evidence.content: All pilot data held by the startup deleted 2026-04-11 under exit annexure clause 4 (simulated).

steps.note: All four milestones are in. The validator can start only now — and was named before any result existed.

steps.action: Cleared the delayed payment and paid milestones 3 and 4
steps.note: Milestone 2 was paid 11 days late; the delay and its reason stay on the record. Payment trace complete.

milestones.1.payment.delay_reason: Budget head re-appropriation pending with the treasury

steps.action: Recomputed the seal and attested the result
steps.note: The validator first recomputes the SHA-256 seal. Only if the criteria are the ones published does it assess the evidence.

validation.method: Difference-in-differences against the comparison OPD; bootstrap 95% CI over daily medians

kpis.kpi: Writes to the HMIS of record

validation.exceptions: 6-hour beacon outage on 2026-02-18 excluded; result unchanged with it included (median 56 min).
validation.attestation: Signed attestation recorded in the signatures table

steps.note: A rules trace, not legal advice from a model: facts, the routes considered, why two were rejected, and who must approve.

facts: Product holds 2 of 3 GeM buyer ratings

accepted.basis: GeM Startup Runway listing procedure, with GFR 173(i) and 170(i) supplying the entry waivers.
accepted.next: This pilot is the second Runway trial; one more buyer rating moves the product to the full GeM catalogue.

rejected.why: Needs the state deeming GR, which is not in force. 'Won our challenge' is not a lawful ground under Rule 166.

rejected.route: Tier 2 — Limited tender to the winners
rejected.why: Only one startup met the criteria; a limited tender needs a cohort of proven winners.

procurement.counterfactual: If the deeming Government Resolution were in force, Tier 1 would be available for this same-department purchase.

steps.note: The purchase is on the record against the evidence that justified it.

deployment.sites: District hospital OPD (pilot site, now permanent)

steps.action: Recorded adoption at 60 days after deployment
steps.note: A pilot that passed but nobody uses is a learning record, not a success. This one is still in use, and the outcome held.

adoption.drop_off: Night-shift registration staff use it least (9 of 14 active)
adoption.outcome_persistence: Median wait 57 min at 60 days (target ≤ 60) — held
adoption.citizen_impact: ≈ 37 minutes saved per OPD visit, ≈ 1,150 visits a day
adoption.unresolved_risks: No owner yet for beacon battery replacement

steps.note: A second department can now read this passport instead of starting from an unverified promise.

replication.decision: Ready for replication through GeM Startup Runway
replication.reusable: Baseline method, sealed KPIs, risk envelope, validator method, exit annexure
replication.remaining_risks: Assign beacon maintenance; re-measure baseline at each new site
